overview:
Texas's 8th District, north of Houston, is an open seat this cycle after Republican Morgan Luttrell chose not to seek re-election. The district carries a R+13 partisan lean, and the 2026 environment points toward the GOP holding the seat. Jessica Hart Steinmann enters the general election with roughly $2.1 million raised and about $1.7 million in outside support, while Democrat Laura Jones has reported about $22,000 in total fundraising. Prediction markets put the chance of a Democratic win near 4 percent.

No public general-election polls are available for this race, so the outlook rests on the district's lean, the fundraising gap, and market pricing. Republicans have held the seat comfortably, and Steinmann is positioned to succeed Luttrell without a serious general-election contest. The absence of polling leaves some residual uncertainty about the exact margin, but the structural evidence points strongly in one direction.
